findings.title: Monitor context builds a translated config copy but returns the untranslated `monitor.config`
findings.description: Line 160 copies the config, and lines 161-162 replace `schedule_type` in that copy with its display name (for example "interval"). The returned dict on line 168 uses `monitor_environment.monitor.config` rather than `config`, so the translated copy is discarded. The event's `contexts.monitor.config.schedule_type` therefore carries the raw integer (`2` for INTERVAL, per `ScheduleType` in src/sentry/monitors/models.py:211-214). The existing test at tests/sentry/monitors/logic/test_mark_failed.py:118-119 asserts `"schedule_type": 2`, so it passes against the defect. A fix will need to update that expectation. The same code was removed verbatim from `mark_failed.py`, so the defect predates this change. It is reported here because the change places it in a new file.

findings.title: Moved logic matches the removed code, and the imports and call sites are consistent
findings.description: I compared the new `try_incident_threshold`, `create_incident_occurrence`, `get_failure_reason`, and `get_monitor_environment_context` with the removed versions in the diff, and only the names differ. Every import kept or added in the four files is used. `types.py` already imports `datetime` and `TypedDict`, so the new `SimpleCheckIn` class resolves. I grepped the repo, and no caller or test references `mark_failed_threshold`, `mark_failed.SimpleCheckIn`, or the old `create_issue_platform_occurrence` name in the monitors package. The `create_issue_platform_occurrence` references in the uptime package are a separate function. The attributes used by the moved code (`get_schedule_type_display`, `get_status_display`, `get_type_display`, `get_last_successful_checkin`, `active_incident`, `grouphash`) all exist on the models.
